To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) face recognition systems are more accurate than humans on images taken in uncontrolled indoor and outdoor settings, (2) the superiority of machines over humans is most pronounced on images taken under favorable conditions, and (3) the advantage of machines over humans in challenging conditions is small.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of face recognition systems that can perform well under a variety of challenging conditions.
the development and evaluation of computer algorithms for face recognition.
developing and applying computational methods to understand and model human face processing and recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
machines are better than humans on frontal images under a wide range of illumination and appearance conditions, but not necessarily better than humans on the most difficult of these conditions.
machines and humans are about equal on challenging face recognition tasks.
machines are superior to humans in the identification of faces from frontal view images under a variety of challenging illumination conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the algorithms are better in the good conditions and the humans are better in the bad conditions.
humans and algorithms perform comparably in the worst case, and that the algorithms are more accurate than humans for most conditions.
face recognition algorithms are now able to perform at a human level for the most difficult frontal face recognition tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of face recognition algorithms can be directly compared with that of humans, and that this can provide insight into the relative importance of different sources of variability in human and machine recognition.

face recognition systems have the potential to perform as well as humans in many real-world applications, but that the performance of face recognition systems is not always better than that of humans.
face recognition algorithms can be used to estimate the difficulty of a face identification task.
